rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model is competitive. config_001 tests the minimal RNA baseline using single-profile PCA, isolating representation quality without confounding multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. This provides a strong reference point to decide whether to exploit RNA, shift to image-only, or invest in multimodal settings later in the budget.

The only completed result is a single-profile RNA PCA baseline with validation accuracy 0.485, leaving major uncertainty about whether the image modality is informative. This experiment tests an image-only ResNet50 single-profile baseline, keeping the design simple and avoiding simultaneous changes to fusion or aggregation. Establishing whether image features are competitive with or complementary to RNA is the most important next uncertainty to resolve, because it determines whether multimodal configurations should be prioritized in the remaining budget.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is currently the strongest result (0.485 acc), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (0.208 acc), so RNA is the more promising direction. The main uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the best RNA encoder without changing the representation. config_002 keeps the proven rna_only + pca_n2000 setting and adds only multiprofile with simple avgpool, making it a minimal test of profile/aggregation effects. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest modality, reduces uncertainty about a central design choice, and will inform whether to pursue transformer aggregation or other RNA encoders next.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool (config_002) substantially outperforms RNA-only singleprofile PCA (config_001), while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool in the currently best RNA multiprofile setting. config_003 changes only aggregation, isolating that effect and clarifying which RNA profile aggregation should be carried into later multimodal tests.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool, which reaches 0.591 accuracy and 0.573 F1, clearly above singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA under this same favorable profile/aggregation setting. config_008 tests scGPT with multiprofile avgpool while holding model setting, profile setting, and aggregation fixed, so it directly exploits the current best direction and isolates the effect of RNA representation. This is a high-value use of the next experiment because it can either produce a new best RNA-only result or confirm PCA, guiding later multimodal and fusion choices with the remaining budget.

The strongest evidence so far is config_002, RNA-only PCA with multiprofile and avgpool, which has the best accuracy (0.591) and F1 (0.573), outperforming single-profile PCA, transformer aggregation, and scGPT avgpool. The key remaining RNA-only uncertainty is whether scvi_n200 can improve on PCA under the same multiprofile avgpool setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder, so it cleanly tests representation quality before adding multimodal or fusion complexity. With 4 experiments left, this one-factor comparison is a high-value step: if scVI improves, it becomes a new best direction; if not, PCA remains the preferred RNA representation and the budget can shift to multimodal extensions.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), and avgpool has outperformed transformer for PCA, so this RNA setting should be kept. The key uncertainty is whether image features can complement the best RNA representation, especially using the stronger untested imagenet_vit_l encoder. This experiment tests that by adding imagenet_vit_l to the proven scvi/multiprofile/avgpool RNA setting with weighted fusion, which can downweight a potentially weak image stream. It is the best next use of the budget because it directly extends the current best configuration toward the highest-ceiling option while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed; if it helps, remaining experiments can refine fusion or aggregation, and if it does not, the search can fall back to RNA-only extensions.

The best result so far is config_037 (0.7062 accuracy, 0.6671 F1), which extends the strong RNA-only evidence that scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is effective and shows that adding a ViT-L image modality can improve performance. The key untested choice in this top-performing family is fusion: weighted versus concat. config_036 keeps the same strong representation and aggregation settings while changing only fusion to concat, isolating the effect of fusion. With only two experiments remaining, this is a high-value exploitation step: if concat improves accuracy, it directly provides a new best configuration; if not, it confirms weighted fusion and leaves one run to test a different aggregation setting.

The strongest evidence is config_036, a multimodal multiprofile model using scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with avgpool and concat fusion, which has the best validation accuracy so far at 0.715 and also outperforms the weighted-fusion counterpart. The key remaining uncertainty in this top-performing block is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool while keeping the stronger concat fusion. config_038 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, directly testing a logical extension of the current best configuration. With only one experiment remaining afterward, this is the best use of the next run because it exploits the most promising direction and has the clearest chance of improving the final best validation accuracy.

The strongest evidence is concentrated in multimodal multiprofile models using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l, with config_038 currently best at 0.7207 accuracy. Within this family, concat outperformed weighted under avgpool, and transformer concat improved accuracy slightly over avgpool concat but had a small F1 drop. The remaining uncertainty is whether weighted fusion can work better with transformer aggregation. config_039 tests exactly this missing corner by changing only fusion from concat to weighted relative to the current best, making it the most targeted exploitation of the most promising region and the best final-budget experiment.
